newsitem.title: MEXICO: Telmex up on rate hikes, ratings change.
newsitem.headline: Telmex up on rate hikes, ratings change.

text.p: Shares in Mexican telephone firm Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) were sharply higher in early trade on Monday amid optimism over a recent hike in local rates for the former monopoly, analysts and dealers said.
Telmex's benchmark L shares were up 6.30 percent to 13.84 pesos on the Mexican bourse and its ADRs were up 2 to 35-3/8.

CS First Boston on Monday raised Telmex to a buy from a hold and Morgan Stanley raised its 1997 and 1998 earnings estimates for the company. Both brokerages said higher local rates that took place on January 1 were a factor.
"People are finally taking notice of (the local tariff increases) and analysts are raising their target price on the stock," said Rizwan Ali, an analyst at Bear Stearns.
Telmex recently won approval by the government to raise its local monthly rent and price of local calls by roughly 50 percent, while basic residential rent rose by some 34 percent.
The local rate increases will probably far outstrip expected inflation of about 18 percent this year in Mexico, although Telmex had seen real local rates fall in the previous few years.

Analysts are also taking a second look at Telmex's ability to face competition that begins in earnest this year. Telmex's moves last year to cut rates and attack its would-be rivals have led some to believe fears of its demise were overblown.
"We continue to believe the stock is attractively valued at current levels and that fears of competition are overdone," Morgan Stanley said in a report.

"The competition at first look does not appear as fearsome as you would have imagined," Bear Stearns' Ali added. He said he expected Telmex to lose between 10 to 14 percent of the lucrative long-distance market.
Local dealers said foreign investors noted Telmex's improved outlook and attractive price while shopping around for good bargains after the holidays.
"Part of this is new year buying by foreign investors," said a trader at Bancomer brokerage.
Dealers also said they were also encouraged by news Telmex repurchased 1.5 percent of its shares from SBC Communications last week.
"Now that looks like a good investment," a local dealer said.
